briefing.text: CALR driver mutations in MPN are exon 9 insertions/deletions that shift the reading frame (type 1 = 52-bp deletion, p.L367fs; type 2 = 5-bp TTGTC insertion, p.K385fs; plus many other +1 frameshift indels). They are not SNVs. If you filter for missense changes or one HGVS string, you will miss them. Select every Hugo_Symbol == CALR row and tabulate Variant_Classification (Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del, ...), Start_Position (GRCh37 chr19 around 13,054,5xx) and HGVSp_Short.
briefing.reason: A naive search for CALR mutations can return zero and wrongly support the hypothesis.

briefing.text: Not every CALR variant is a driver. Only somatic +1 frameshift indels in exon 9 that change the C-terminus are pathogenic. In-frame exon 9 deletions and point mutations may be non-functional or germline polymorphisms. Classify each CALR row: frameshift or in-frame, and check somatic status (Mutation_Status, normal alt counts) if those columns exist. Base the conclusion on somatic frameshift CALR mutations, and report other CALR variants separately.
briefing.reason: This decides which CALR calls count as the 'somatic CALR mutations' the hypothesis is about.

briefing.text: 'JAK2 nonmutated' does not mean 'no JAK2 V617F'. JAK2 exon 12 mutations (e.g. N542-E543del, K539L) and other JAK2 drivers also make a patient JAK2-mutated. List every JAK2 row by HGVSp_Short and Variant_Classification. Use 'no JAK2 driver' as the main definition and report the stricter 'no JAK2 mutation of any kind' too.
briefing.reason: The definition of the JAK2-nonmutated group changes who counts toward the hypothesis.

briefing.text: JAK2 and CALR mutations are mostly mutually exclusive, but a few percent of MPN patients carry both, often with a low-VAF JAK2 V617F subclone. A patient with both mutations is JAK2-mutated and is not evidence about the JAK2-nonmutated group. Cross-tabulate JAK2 against CALR. For patients with both, check JAK2 VAF = t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count). Check that the conclusion holds both with and without low-VAF JAK2 calls.
briefing.reason: Patients with both mutations must not be counted as JAK2-nonmutated, and low-VAF JAK2 calls should be tested for their effect on the result.

briefing.text: Samples with no mutation calls do not appear in data_mutations.txt. Build the cohort and the JAK2-nonmutated group from data_clinical_sample.txt: all clinical samples minus samples with a JAK2 mutation. Compare the clinical SAMPLE_IDs with the unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode values in the mutation file.
briefing.reason: Without this, the JAK2-nonmutated group and its denominator are built wrongly.

briefing.text: Check that Tumor_Sample_Barcode in the mutation file matches SAMPLE_ID in the clinical table, and check whether any patient has more than one sample. The hypothesis is about patients, so set mutation status per patient: a patient is JAK2-mutated if any of their samples is.
briefing.reason: Joining on the wrong ID, or splitting one patient across several samples, can make JAK2-nonmutated assignments wrong.

briefing.text: The hypothesis is a universal negative ('not present in any patient'). One somatic CALR driver mutation in one JAK2-nonmutated patient contradicts it. A mutual-exclusivity test or a low frequency is the wrong evidence. The quantity to report is the number of patients who have a CALR driver mutation and no JAK2 mutation. The claim can only be supported if that count is zero and CALR was actually covered by the sequencing.
briefing.reason: This sets the decision logic. Without it, a team might run significance tests that do not answer an 'any' claim.

shared_assumptions: JAK2 status is taken as 'no JAK2 row in the MAF'. Neither team tested whether a sample with no calls (team A found one) or a sample sequenced on a limited panel really counts as JAK2-nonmutated rather than unknown.
Every CALR row is treated as somatic because SOMATIC_STATUS is 'Matched'. Neither team tied that to the per-row germline read counts or allele percentages.
The cohort is taken to be all MPN samples, with no split by subtype or by MPL status, even though some samples are flagged as MPL-mutated.
unused_evidence: Team B did not use the study's 'JAK2/MPL mutation' column (values JAK2 / MPL / unmutated), which records the study's own per-sample driver status. Team A used it.

Team B did not use the 'Germline allele percentage (%)' and 'Germline reads' columns. Team A found that 7 of 25 CALR rows had nonzero germline percentages but did not check whether those rows have enough germline depth to call them somatic.
MPL rows (7) and the MPL flag were not used to define a 'JAK2-nonmutated' group that excludes or includes MPL-mutated cases.
TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS was not used. It probably does not matter here.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named possible undetected low-VAF JAK2 as their weakest point. Neither resolved it. Team A could not compute VAF from t_ref/t_alt but did not use the 'Tumor allele burden (%)' column that is present.
Team A noted that 7 CALR calls have germline allele % up to 33% and only argued them away. It did not run a depth-based check.
second_readings: 'Nonmutated JAK2' could mean JAK2-unmutated only, or 'neither JAK2 nor MPL mutated' (triple-negative framing). The answer should hold under both readings.
'Patients' versus samples: if a patient had several samples, the count unit would matter. Team A reports one sample per patient.
challenge.verdict: High trust. The hypothesis is a universal negative, and both teams report many CALR exon 9 frameshifts in samples with no JAK2 call. Plausible problems (germline CALR calls, missed low-burden JAK2, MPL scope) would have to remove every such case to flip the answer. That is unlikely, but it has not been fully checked.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: For the 7 CALR rows with nonzero germline allele %, tabulate Germline reads and germline allele % against Tumor allele burden (%). Do any rows look more consistent with a germline variant than with tumour contamination, and does dropping them change your count or label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You said JAK2 VAF could not be computed, but a 'Tumor allele burden (%)' column exists. Does the JAK2 allele-burden distribution show any very-low-burden JAK2 calls, and does it change your view that there is no JAK2/CALR overlap?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Does the CALR-positive, JAK2-nonmutated count change if you also exclude MPL-mutated samples (using MPL rows and the JAK2/MPL column)? Does the label hold under both readings of 'nonmutated JAK2'?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Cross-tabulate your MAF-derived JAK2 status against the study's 'JAK2/MPL mutation' column for every CALR-positive sample. Do the two agree, and does any disagreement change the method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: SOMATIC_STATUS 'Matched' is a per-sample label. Check the per-row 'Germline reads' and 'Germline allele percentage (%)' for every CALR call. Are any CALR calls plausibly germline, and does excluding them change your conclusion?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: How did you treat clinical-table samples with no mutation calls at all, which leaves their JAK2 status unknown rather than nonmutated? Also, does the CALR-positive count change when MPL-mutated samples are excluded from the JAK2-nonmutated group?

questions.why: This would settle whether CALR calls with nonzero germline reads can still be counted as somatic.

findings.question: In matched tumour-normal myeloid sequencing, what germline allele fraction and germline depth thresholds are conventionally used to tell tumour-in-normal contamination from a true germline variant?
findings.answer: No single myeloid-specific convention exists; the web gives tool defaults and a guiding principle. Principle (Barnell et al. 2018 SOP, Genet Med): a germline variant shows normal-sample VAF near 50% or 100%, with read support in the normal beyond what tumour contamination can explain. Tumour-in-normal contamination instead gives a low normal VAF, well below the tumour VAF. Genomics England (Nat Commun 2024) reports contamination is common in MPN sorted CD3+ T cells and in saliva, which causes true driver hotspots to be wrongly subtracted. Caller thresholds: MuTect1 rejects a call if the normal has >=2 alt reads or >=3% alt fraction (with base-quality sum >20). MuTect2 (GATK 3.7) defaults to at most 1 alt read and a 0.03 fraction in the normal; for deep panels these are commonly relaxed to a 0.10 normal fraction, plus a rule that tumour AF must exceed 4x normal AF (S_AF>0.75). DRAGEN's alt_allele_in_normal filter fires above 0.2 normal VAF plus a contamination tolerance of 0.15 in liquid-tumour mode (0 in solid mode), so the cutoff is 0.35 for haematological samples. DRAGEN also ignores normal artifacts when normal AF < 0.1x tumour AF. Practical reading: a CALR call with a few normal reads at low normal VAF (roughly <10%, and tumour VAF >=4-10x normal VAF) is conventionally treated as contamination and still counted as somatic. A normal VAF of about 40-60% (or about 100%) indicates germline. The pages read give no conventional germline-depth threshold beyond caller minimum-read rules.
